content.text:
`fetchUser` (`src/user.js:1-13`) retries `api.get` up to `retries` times (default 2, so 3 attempts total). Each `TimeoutError` is caught and swallowed via `continue`; any other error is rethrown. If every attempt times out, the loop exits normally and line 12 falls through to `return {}` — that's a hardcoded fallback, not something the timeout itself produces directly.

This design is risky for callers: a timed-out fetch is indistinguishable from a real "empty user" response, since nothing signals that the call failed (no error, no `null`, no status flag). Any caller checking `user.id` or similar will silently misbehave instead of seeing a clear failure. Worth reconsidering — throw after exhausting retries, or return `null`/a discriminated result — depending on how callers are meant to handle a fetch failure.
